Noted — **backoff plus circuit breaker**. That means the full-jitter loop above stays as-is, wrapped in a breaker that trips `OPEN` on sustained failure and fails fast until a half-open probe succeeds.

Two parameters to pin down when we implement: the trip threshold (I'd default to a 50% failure rate over a 20-request rolling window rather than a raw consecutive-failure count) and the `OPEN` duration before the half-open probe (30s). The good news:

- Videos are browser-compatible H.264, 720×1280, 30 fps.
- Every video has fast-start metadata.
- Progressive MP4 is sufficient; these clips are too short to justify HLS.
- The upload script already uses a public Supabase bucket and one-year browser caching. Public assets receive better CDN cache behavior. [Supabase CDN documentation](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/cdn/fundamentals)

Before deployment, I recommend:

- Cap every video around 2–2.5 Mbps.
- Reduce the toe-and-heel clip to roughly 2–2.5 MB.
- Reduce the opener to roughly 2.5–3 MB.
- Convert the countdown to approximately 50–80 KB AAC/MP3.
- Convert the music into a seamless 96 kbps loop instead of a 24 MB master.
- Preload the countdown sound when the player opens.
- Test the deployed session under throttled “Slow 4G.”

That should reduce the session package to approximately 30–35 MB and make it comfortably streamable. Supabase Storage routes requests through its CDN, and public buckets produce stronger cache-hit rates. [Supabase public asset guidance](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/serving/downloads)

sessions.title: Supabase branching with worktrees
sessions.lastUserText: does supabase support branching? so the changes in a worktree does not affect other branches of the database?

last.text:
**Yes, Supabase supports branching** — preview branches (ephemeral, tied to a PR) and persistent branches (long-lived, for staging/dev). Each gets its own isolated Postgres instance.

**But it wouldn't fix your problem**, for four reasons specific to this repo:

| Requirement | This project |
|---|---|
| Branches a **hosted** Supabase project | Dev points at `localhost:5432/fiftystrong_dev` — local Postgres |
| Needs a git remote for the GitHub integration | **No remote at all** — `git remote -v` is empty |
| Needs `supabase/` with the CLI config | No `supabase/` directory; `@supabase/supabase-js` is only used for Storage |
| Branch DBs are built by **replaying migrations** | `drizzle/0000` has **zero** mention of `quiz_responses`, and declares `programme_version text` where the schema has `programme jsonb` |

That last row is the real blocker, and it's worth dwelling on: **a branch database is only as good as your migrations.** Supabase would spin up a fresh Postgres and replay `supabase/migrations/`. This project has none, and its Drizzle baseline is badly stale — so you'd get an empty or wrong database, not a copy of your schema.

The stale migrations are also why `drizzle-kit generate` refused to run non-interactively earlier: it wanted me to resolve a `programme` vs `programme_version` conflict that predates all my work.

## What I'd actually do

**Now — one line, solves it today.** Give this worktree its own local database:

```
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://eugenechan@localhost:5432/fiftystrong_analytics
```

`.env.local` is gitignored and already per-worktree, so `web/` and `web-paywall/` keep the old shape and nothing is shared. I'd seed it from `schema.ts` via `db:push`, not from the broken migrations.

**Soon — fix the migration chain.** Regenerate a Drizzle baseline that matches `schema.ts`, so there's a working path from nothing to a correct database. You currently don't have one. This is a prerequisite for Supabase branching *and* for onboarding a second machine *and* for any production deploy that isn't `db:push` against live data.

**Later — branching, if it earns its place.** It's genuinely good once migrations work, and the persistent-branch flavour would suit a staging environment. But it's solving "isolate hosted environments per PR", and today you have one developer, no remote, and no hosted dev project.

One caveat on the above: I couldn't get current pricing or the exact migration prerequisite from the docs page — it says "deploy directly from GitHub on any plan" but doesn't state per-branch cost. Worth checking before committing to it, since branch instances bill by the hour on most tiers.

Want me to point this worktree at its own database, or start on the migration baseline?

sessions.title: Frequent cellular disconnections
sessions.lastUserText: is the issue mostly because we are connected using tailscale? and tailscale is not stable when the phone is on cellular network?

last.text:
Confirmed — so here's the calibrated answer.

**Yes, the transport is the cause. Not the server, not the app's logic.** The proof that doesn't depend on any lfg code: during a bad window, `tailscale ping` from the Mac to your phone timed out 5/5. That probe never touches lfg. When the tunnel isn't passing packets, nothing in the client can help.

**But "cellular" isn't quite the variable.** Two corrections to the obvious reading:

**1. `grade=relayed` in the log is not a Tailscale fact.** `PathQuality.swift:96` assigns that label purely from RTT — over ~200ms and lfg calls it "relayed." It's a guess used to size timeouts. It is not the client observing DERP. So you can't read the log and conclude "Tailscale relayed me."

**2. It fails on Wi-Fi too.** `20:53–20:55` was `ifaces=wifi,wifi,cellular`, not expensive — and the stream still died at `20:54:39` with the keepalive failing alongside it. So the variable is path *quality*, not the radio.

**The most diagnostic line is one that's in every log entry, including the dead stretches:** `other(utun9)`. That's the Tailscale interface, and it's present throughout the blackouts. So the tunnel isn't being torn down by iOS — the interface is up the whole time and simply carries nothing. That points at Tailscale's data path (path re-punch, DERP failover, carrier NAT rebinding) rather than the extension being suspended.

Ground truth right now, from this Mac:

```
iphone-13-pro    direct via 112.118.220.27:41641   176ms
macbook-air      DERP(hkg) ×5 — "direct connection not established"
```

Your phone currently holds a **direct** path. Cellular is where direct paths are hardest to keep — carrier CGNAT gives you no stable port, so the path needs re-punching every time the binding expires, and each re-punch is a window where packets vanish. That's why it's worse on cellular without being exclusive to it.

**So: the drops are Tailscale's path, and cellular makes them frequent.** What lfg controls is only how gracefully it rides that out — which is what the `202608162108` fix addresses, and why it reduces drops rather than eliminating them.

**The one thing that would settle it:** next time the app shows disconnected, open the Tailscale app and check whether it says the Pro is connected via a relay. If it also looks broken there, it's confirmed at the Tailscale layer and worth a bug report to them — captured *before* you toggle the VPN, since toggling repairs it and erases the evidence.
